Mariæ Ma-joris, ad aram faciens, structis insidiis captus, & munitissimâ in turre in carcerem conditus: & Gela „ suis 11. pedes ligatus per Romana compita tractus & fœdissimè tractatus fuit. Hâc inductione usus auctor, egregiè mihi illustrat, ut potentia Principum secularis huic hominum generi non aliter respiciatur, quam ut manus mali; adversus quam munienda erat sedes Romana: quare rota[?] hæc inductio in argumentum adducitur, quo Bonifacium suum justificare ex consilio laborat. Ita enim conclusionem facturus, pergit.

page.notes: The printed quotation marks (,,) stand at the start of each line and are transcribed where they stand. The reading "cæsufque" is doubtful. The scan shows a small dot below the last line at the right. It is not text and is left out. The quotation marks („) at the start of lines are printed and are kept. "Gela" is printed in italic at the line end, and the following word "suis" is italic at the start of the next line; the word is unclear, so it is not marked. The word before "hæc" is "rota" or "tota", and I could not tell which, so it is marked [?]. The catchword "mâ" is the start of the next page's first word; a quotation mark stands before it in the scan and is not included.
